stories.title: Pope Leo says concerns about AI doom scenarios are not ‘fake news’

en.title: Pope Leo says concerns about AI doom scenarios are not 'fake news'
en.summary: Pope Leo stated that concerns about artificial intelligence potentially causing global harm deserve serious consideration, appearing to contradict US President Donald Trump. The pontiff also directly criticized technology CEOs who oppose implementing safeguards on AI development.

stories.title: In the US-China AI race, the real fight is keeping humans in control

en.title: In the US-China AI race, the real fight is keeping humans in control
en.summary: The US and China compete for AI dominance as a source of economic and strategic advantage, creating tension between rapid development and maintaining human oversight. A recent Trump-Xi summit highlighted their differing approaches to AI regulation and control.

stories.title: China pledges to ‘firmly support’ Cuba as US escalates pressure on Havana

en.title: China pledges to 'firmly support' Cuba as US escalates pressure on Havana
en.summary: China committed to supporting Cuba's sovereignty and resisting outside interference, according to a foreign ministry spokesman marking 66 years of diplomatic relations. The statement came as the US increases pressure on Cuba's government.

stories.title: US revokes visas from Latin American officials and families over accusations of corruption

en.title: US revokes visas from Latin American officials and families over accusations of corruption
en.summary: The Trump administration revoked visas for 27 Latin American officials and their families from Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru citing corruption allegations. The affected nations all have right-leaning governments aligned with the US.

stories.title: JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon on how growth can untangle US-China strife, thorny global issues

en.title: JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon on how growth can untangle US-China strife, thorny global issues
en.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon recently visited Hong Kong for meetings with business leaders and entrepreneurs, demonstrating his growing public engagement with global economic and geopolitical matters beyond financial industry strategy.

stories.title: French far-right’s Bardella denies alleged antisemitic comments, files defamation lawsuit

en.title: French far-right's Bardella denies alleged antisemitic comments, files defamation lawsuit
en.summary: A French investigative website alleged that far-right National Rally leader Jordan Bardella made antisemitic comments in a 2013 chat. Bardella denied the claims as fabricated and filed a defamation lawsuit in response.

stories.title: Putin signs decree adding 15,500 troops to Russian army

en.title: Putin signs decree adding 15,500 troops to Russian army
en.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree increasing the armed forces by 15,500 personnel to a total of 2,441,630 troops. This is the fourth such troop increase order issued this year amid ongoing casualties in the Ukraine war.

stories.title: US to grant sanctions waiver for flights between Iran and Iraq’s Najaf, source says

en.title: US to grant sanctions waiver for flights between Iran and Iraq's Najaf, source says
en.summary: The Trump administration plans to grant a limited waiver to Iran sanctions allowing Iraqi Airways to operate flights between Iran and the Iraqi city of Najaf for Shiite religious pilgrims. The waiver would initially last one month with potential extension.

stories.title: Trump unveils US$15 billion Iowa steel project the White House says will be biggest in US

en.title: Trump unveils US$15 billion Iowa steel project the White House says will be biggest in US
en.summary: President Trump announced a Minnesota-based company's plan to construct a US$15 billion steel mill in Iowa, which the White House describes as the largest manufacturing investment of its kind in the country.

stories.title: FBI deputy chief Andrew Bailey to resign after a little more than a year with agency

en.title: FBI deputy chief Andrew Bailey to resign after a little more than a year with agency
en.summary: Andrew Bailey, the FBI's deputy director and a Republican ally of President Trump, is resigning from his position after serving for just over a year to return to his family.

stories.title: （爱知·名古屋亚运会）综合消息：中国乒乓球队6金收官 中国队卫冕田径男、女4X100米接力

en.title: (Aichi Nagoya Asian Games) Summary: China's table tennis team finishes with 6 gold medals; China retains men's and women's 4x100m relay athletics titles
en.summary: China's table tennis team won six gold medals across seven events at the Aichi Nagoya Asian Games, claiming the men's singles and women's doubles titles on the final day. China also successfully defended both the men's and women's 4x100 meter relay athletics championships.

stories.title: VW, Gotion ramp up battery production in Europe, Morocco amid rising EV demand

en.title: VW, Gotion ramp up battery production in Europe, Morocco amid rising EV demand
en.summary: Volkswagen Group and Chinese battery maker Gotion High-tech plan to invest €3.22 billion to establish three production lines in Europe and North Africa, targeting a combined capacity of 37.5 gigawatt hours of lithium-ion batteries.

stories.title: China is no longer just the world’s factory. It’s the HQ

en.title: China is no longer just the world's factory. It's the HQ
en.summary: China's role in global electronics manufacturing is shifting as its concentrated supply chains disperse, but the country is retaining control of core industrial capabilities while exporting manufacturing processes.

stories.title: AIIB plans to double financing by 2030. Can it bridge Asia’s infrastructure gap?

en.title: AIIB plans to double financing by 2030. Can it bridge Asia's infrastructure gap?
en.summary: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank aims to double its annual financing to approximately US$20 billion by 2030 to address growing infrastructure funding needs across member economies.

stories.title: Hong Kong office expansion lags hiring push as tenants optimise current space: Colliers

en.title: Hong Kong office expansion lags hiring push as tenants optimise current space: Colliers
en.summary: Hong Kong office tenants plan to hire more staff over the next year, but few intend to expand their physical office space, instead maximizing efficiency in existing premises.
